study type: Simulation study using retrospective patient data
exposure: Proton therapy delivery methods (Passive Scattering (PS) vs. Pencil-Beam Scanning (PBS))
cohort: The study used treatment and anatomic data obtained from a cohort of children with craniopharyngioma who previously received PS or PBS proton therapy.
finding: The proton delivery method affects dose-weighted average linear energy transfer (LETD) both inside and outside of the target volume, with PBS generally resulting in greater LETD values than PS, suggesting PBS is more biologically effective than PS.
